title: Development charge update and St. Columba lease deferral
subtitle: North Lot sale, Beaver Creek reconstruction contract, King Street North rezoning, and 2025 budget surplus projections.
overview: Council started work on updating the city's development charge by-law. It directed staff to prepare the background study, keep charges uniform across the city, and look into an industrial-specific charge and incentives for higher-density and non-residential development. These charges pay for growth-related infrastructure, so the outcome will affect both new construction and what existing taxpayers cover.

Council deferred a proposed three-year lease of the St. Columba site as an arts space until the next regular meeting {{vote:m11}}. The reasons given were further review of financial information and of zoning and land use questions. Several community delegates had spoken in support of the lease.

Council also awarded a $19,988,579.22 contract for Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction. It approved the sale of part of the North Parking Lot, a related land exchange, and an official plan and zoning amendment for a seven-storey building at King Street North and Columbia Street West. Staff projected a 2025 net tax base surplus of $891,000 and an enterprise surplus of about $638,000, with a follow-up report due in the fall.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to prepare the background study on the growth-related capital program, keep city-wide charges, update the interest policy, and investigate an industrial-specific charge and incentives for higher-density and non-residential development.
Council deferred report CAO2025-020 to the next regular meeting to allow further consideration of financial information and zoning and land use matters {{vote:m11}}.
Council awarded RFT25-04 for Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction to Regional Sewer and Watermain Ltd. for a total of $19,988,579.22 including unrecoverable HST.
Council approved an agreement of purchase and sale with Tricap for a one-acre portion of the North Parking Lot and delegated to the CAO authority to renegotiate the related 2005 parking agreement.
Council approved a land exchange agreement between the City and Atrium Waterloo Limited Partnership and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign it.

decisions.item: 1 Columbia St. W. and King St. N. development
decisions.detail: Council approved Official Plan Amendment 55 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-07 to allow a seven-storey mixed-use building and renovations to the existing 22-storey building.
Council acknowledged a projected 2025 net tax base surplus of $891,000 and enterprise surplus of about $638,000, and asked for a follow-up projection in the fall.
Council approved adding surety bonds as an acceptable form of security and a $475 fee for exchanging existing securities.

debate: On development charges, councillors asked whether area-specific charges would suit the city. The consultant said an earlier exercise found rates close to the city-wide rate, because upgrading existing streets costs more than building in open land. Staff added that city-wide collection gives a larger pool of money and avoids running what would amount to two by-laws.

Councillors questioned the political claims about development charges. Staff said uncommitted reserves were about $5.9 million and already tied to budgeted projects. The consultant said research on whether lower charges reduce housing costs is inconclusive. One councillor noted that high-charge GTA municipalities still see heavy development, and another said a federal pledge to cut charges needs matching funding for municipalities.

Some councillors wanted the project list reviewed again, citing the cost of buried hydro and the removal of items such as libraries. One councillor asked for wider consultation than builders and industry groups, and staff said they would consider it. Staff also noted that growth only partly pays for itself, since operating and replacement costs fall to property taxes.

On St. Columba, delegates from the arts community supported the lease. They cited long waiting lists for studio space, affordability for artists, the record of the proposed operator and neighbourhood support. One councillor who moved the deferral raised budget pressures, the cost of renovating the building, whether the zoning allows the use, and a possible record of site condition requirement. Planning staff said a public service exemption or a temporary use by-law might apply but needed more detail.

Councillors opposing the deferral said council had unanimously approved the purchase and interim use in February, that the funding came from existing reserves with no new tax impact, and that nothing new had been raised by staff. They also said a deferral would signal a lack of support for the arts. The clerk explained that a deferral motion is decided first, as a yes or no vote.
